q: Why do animals store most long-term energy as triglycerides rather than glycogen?
options: Triglycerides are more soluble, so they can be mobilised much faster than glycogen
Triglycerides can be respired anaerobically whenever the oxygen supply to the muscles runs out
Glycogen can never be broken back down into glucose once it has been stored
Fat holds twice the energy per gram and is stored without water, so it's much lighter
explanation: Lipids release ~37 kJ/g versus ~17 kJ/g for carbohydrate, and because they are hydrophobic they are stored without water – whereas glycogen is stored with several times its mass of water. So fat gives far more energy per unit of body mass, vital for mobile animals. Trade-off: glycogen is mobilised faster and can fuel anaerobic respiration.
